scope_in: Learning or computing a policy that acts over time in an environment and is judged by long-run return.
scope_out: Predicting a future value without acting on it goes to modality:Temporal Signals; one-shot ranking or recommendation goes to domain:Information Services.
example_children: Reinforcement Learning; Imitation Learning; Model Predictive Control
notes: Largest method branch in the corpus: Reinforcement Learning alone is 263 papers, the 2nd most frequent name. Eight children is justified by that mass.

scope_in: Algorithms that improve a policy or value function from experience: value-based, policy-gradient, actor-critic, offline, distributional, risk-sensitive, constrained.
scope_out: Work on which experience to collect goes to Exploration in Reinforcement Learning; work on where the reward comes from goes to Learning from Human Feedback.
example_children: Proximal Policy Optimization; Offline Reinforcement Learning; Distributional Reinforcement Learning
notes: Absorbs the many '<adjective> Reinforcement Learning' tail names (safe, robust, risk-averse, maximum-entropy, value-based, model-free).

scope_in: How an agent decides what to try: exploration bonuses, intrinsic motivation, option and skill discovery, reset-free data collection.
scope_out: Exploration/exploitation in stateless bandit settings goes to Sequential Decision Processes.
example_children: Intrinsic Motivation; Skill Discovery; Option Discovery
notes: Small but sharply delimited; kept separate because the corpus has a dedicated vocabulary for it (Cooperative Exploration, Exploration Strategies, Optimization of Intrinsic Rewards).

scope_in: Deriving the objective itself from demonstrations, preferences or human judgement rather than from a coded reward.
scope_out: Instruction-tuning a language model with no learned reward model goes to Training Regimes:Transfer Learning; alignment argued as a normative goal goes to concern:AI Safety.
example_children: Imitation Learning; Inverse Reinforcement Learning; Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
notes: Placed under Sequential Decision-Making rather than under Training Regimes because in this corpus every instance is about acquiring a reward or policy for an acting agent.

scope_in: Several learning agents in a shared environment: credit assignment across agents, coordination, centralised-training regimes, emergent communication.
scope_out: Distributing one model’s training across machines goes to Training Regimes:Federated Learning; equilibria analysed rather than learned go to Game-Theoretic Modelling.
example_children: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning; Centralized Training Decentralized Execution (CTDE); Language Emergence

scope_in: Equilibria, incentives, mechanism and auction design and welfare objectives, analysed as games.
scope_out: Agents that acquire behaviour by interaction go to Multi-Agent Learning; economics as a field of application goes to domain:Economics.
example_children: Game Theory; Cooperative Game Theory; Coordination Games
notes: Game Theory has 20 papers; it sits here because in this corpus it is almost always about strategic interaction between decision-makers.

scope_in: The decision formalism itself and its properties: MDPs, POMDPs, bandits, partial monitoring, bisimulation.
scope_out: A new algorithm merely evaluated on these formalisms goes to Policy Learning Algorithms.
example_children: Markov Decision Processes; Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes; Contextual Bandits

scope_in: Stability, feedback and optimal control for dynamics that are known or separately identified.
scope_out: Learning the dynamics model itself goes to Dynamical Systems Modelling:System Identification; robot hardware stacks go to domain:Robotics.
example_children: Optimal Control; Control Systems; Lyapunov Stability

scope_in: Search over a model of the world to choose actions: motion and task planning, probabilistic planning, dynamic programming, planning with a learned model.
scope_out: Executing a plan on a physical platform goes to domain:Robotics; planning as an LLM reasoning behaviour goes to modality:Language Model Behaviour.
example_children: Motion Planning; Probabilistic Planning; Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
notes: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning is placed here, not in Policy Learning Algorithms, because its distinguishing act is planning against a learned model. Reviewers may disagree.

scope_in: The design and analysis of algorithms that minimise an objective, and the formulation of decisions as objectives.
scope_out: A statement that a model was 'optimised' for a task carries no method and goes to Not Specified; proofs about learning rather than about an algorithm go to Learning Theory.
example_children: Optimization; Combinatorial Optimization; Stochastic Optimization
notes: Optimization (71 papers) plus a very deep tail of named algorithms; the second-largest method branch.

scope_in: Gradient and proximal methods over continuous variables: stochastic, adaptive, accelerated, distributed, bi-level, minimax, variational-inequality.
scope_out: Methods studied specifically for the behaviour of neural-network training go to Deep Learning Optimization.
example_children: Stochastic Gradient Descent; Stochastic Mirror Descent; First-Order Methods

scope_in: Problems over discrete structures: integer and mixed-integer programming, routing, scheduling, constraint and satisfiability solving, and learned heuristics for them.
scope_out: Continuous relaxations go to Continuous Optimization Algorithms; the industry the instance comes from goes to the domain axis.
example_children: Combinatorial Optimization; Mixed-Integer Linear Programming; Vehicle Routing Problem
notes: Deliberately absorbs the operations-research vocabulary (Operations Research, 19 papers; Personnel Scheduling; Facility Location). I did not create an operations-research domain: OR names get method=Discrete Optimization and, where stated, a domain such as Transportation Systems.

scope_in: Objectives whose data are random or adversarial: stochastic programming, robust and distributionally robust formulations, contextual optimisation.
scope_out: Uncertainty in a model’s predictions goes to concern:Uncertainty Quantification; robustness of a trained model to shifted inputs goes to concern:Robustness to Distribution Shift.
example_children: Stochastic Programming; Robust Optimization; Conditional Robust Optimization

scope_in: Searching a design or configuration space with no usable gradient: Bayesian optimisation, evolutionary search, metaheuristics, architecture and hyper-parameter search.
scope_out: Gradient-based parameter fitting goes to Continuous Optimization Algorithms.
example_children: Bayesian Optimization; Hyper-Parameter Optimization; Neural Architecture Search
notes: Neural Architecture Search is filed here rather than under Neural Architecture Design: its contribution is the search procedure, not the architecture.

scope_in: The empirical behaviour of neural-network training: loss landscapes, training dynamics, implicit regularisation, batch-size and schedule effects, initialisation.
scope_out: Making training cheaper or more parallel goes to concern:Computational Efficiency; bounds on the resulting generalisation go to Learning Theory.
example_children: Training Dynamics; Loss Landscape Analysis; Sharpness-Aware Minimization

scope_in: Building a model of a distribution and computing with it: generative models, posterior inference, graphical structure, sampling.
scope_out: Reporting a predictive uncertainty number as the contribution goes to concern:Uncertainty Quantification; point-estimate predictors go to Classical Machine Learning Methods.
example_children: Generative Models; Bayesian Inference; Variational Inference
notes: Generative Models (83 papers) sits here rather than on an architecture axis: the corpus quotes use it to name a modelling goal, not a network.

scope_in: Neural models of a data distribution and the objectives that train them: diffusion, flows, autoencoding, energy-based, score-based, adversarial, GFlowNets.
scope_out: What is generated (images, molecules, text) is recorded on the modality axis, not here.
example_children: Diffusion Models; Normalizing Flows; Energy-based Models
notes: The single largest concentration of tail names in the corpus after the RL family.

scope_in: Computing or approximating posteriors: variational methods, MCMC, amortised and simulation-based inference, Bayesian deep learning.
scope_out: Bayesian optimisation used as a search strategy goes to Optimization:Black-Box Optimization.
example_children: Variational Inference; Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC); Simulation-Based Inference

scope_in: Models whose contribution is an explicit dependence structure over variables: Bayesian networks, latent-variable and state-space structure, structure learning.
scope_out: Learning on graphs that are themselves the data (citation, molecular, social) goes to modality:Graph-Structured Data.
example_children: Graphical Models; Latent Variable Models; Bayesian Networks
notes: The scope_out line matters: 'graph' in this corpus far more often means the data than the model.

scope_in: Sampling-based simulation of random processes, and the process models behind it.
scope_out: Domain simulators used only as a data source (radiation transport, N-body, crowd) go to the domain axis.
example_children: Monte Carlo Simulations; Stochastic Processes; Temporal Point Processes
notes: Least certain child of this branch; Monte Carlo names in this corpus split between generic sampling and medical-physics dose simulation.

scope_in: How supervision, tasks and data availability are arranged across training — not what is learned, and not with which model.
scope_out: Making training cheaper goes to concern:Computational Efficiency; constructing or cleaning the data goes to Data-Centric Machine Learning; properties of the resulting latent space go to Representation Learning.
example_children: Self-Supervised Learning; Transfer Learning; Continual Learning
notes: Bare Supervised Learning / Classification / Regression names attach to this level directly, with no child.

scope_in: Training on a signal derived from unlabelled data itself: contrastive, predictive and masked pretext objectives, pretraining without labels.
scope_out: What the resulting embedding is like goes to Representation Learning; using someone else’s pretrained model goes to Transfer Learning.
example_children: Contrastive Learning; Self-Supervised Learning (SSL); Language Model Pre-training
notes: Overlaps Representation Learning by construction; the split is signal (here) versus latent structure (there). This is one of my least confident boundaries.

scope_in: Reusing a model trained on one distribution or task for another: fine-tuning, domain adaptation, cross-lingual and sim-to-real transfer, zero- and few-shot use.
scope_out: Generalising to shifted test data with no target-domain training stage goes to concern:Robustness to Distribution Shift; cheap adapters as the contribution go to concern:Efficient Fine-Tuning.
example_children: Domain Adaptation; Sim-to-Real Transfer; Cross-lingual Transfer

scope_in: Learning from a non-stationary stream of tasks without losing what was learned before.
scope_out: Adapting once to a new domain goes to Transfer Learning; detecting that the stream has shifted goes to concern:Robustness to Distribution Shift.
example_children: Catastrophic Forgetting; Class-Incremental Learning; Online Continual Learning

scope_in: Learning a learning procedure, initialisation or parameter generator from a distribution of tasks.
scope_out: Pretrain-then-finetune with no task distribution goes to Transfer Learning.
example_children: Few-Shot Learning; Meta-gradient Learning; Hypernetworks

scope_in: Training one model on several objectives at once, and the interference and weighting problems that creates.
scope_out: One objective over several data types goes to modality:Multimodal Data; sequential rather than simultaneous tasks go to Continual Learning.
example_children: Multi-Task Learning; Multi-Objective Learning; Auxiliary Tasks

scope_in: Training across data holders that never pool their data: aggregation, client heterogeneity, decentralised protocols.
scope_out: Multi-machine training for throughput inside one datacentre goes to concern:Training Scalability; a formal privacy guarantee as the contribution goes to concern:Privacy.
example_children: Federated Learning; Decentralized Learning; Communication-Efficient Learning

scope_in: Training when labels are partial, noisy, indirect or imbalanced.
scope_out: No labels at all goes to Self-Supervised Learning; repairing labels in a released dataset goes to Data-Centric Machine Learning:Data Quality Management.
example_children: Semi-Supervised Learning; Learning with Noisy Labels; Weak Supervision

scope_in: Reaching a target performance from fewer examples by choosing or ordering them: active learning, curriculum, sample-complexity-driven selection.
scope_out: Making each training step cheaper goes to concern:Computational Efficiency; formal sample-complexity results go to Learning Theory.
example_children: Active Learning; Curriculum Learning; Sample Efficiency

scope_in: Predictors and decompositions that do not depend on deep networks: kernels, ensembles, clustering, factorisation, classical regression and estimation.
scope_out: Deep predictors go to Neural Architecture Design or Not Specified; theory about any predictor goes to Learning Theory.
example_children: Support Vector Machines; Gaussian Processes; Ensemble Learning
notes: Kept as a branch because ~60 tail names in this corpus name a pre-deep-learning method, mostly from biomedical and environmental collaborations.

scope_in: Learning through a similarity function: SVMs, Gaussian processes, kernels on structured objects.
scope_out: The Neural Tangent Kernel as an analysis device goes to Learning Theory:Expressivity of Neural Networks.
example_children: Support Vector Machines; Gaussian Processes; Graph Kernels

scope_in: Combining many predictors: bagging, boosting, deep ensembles, model averaging and merging.
scope_out: Ensembles used to produce uncertainty estimates go to concern:Uncertainty Quantification.
example_children: Ensemble Methods; Boosting Algorithms; Model Averaging

scope_in: Finding structure with no target variable: clustering, dimensionality reduction, manifold and spectral methods, matrix and tensor factorisation, ICA.
scope_out: Deep latent-variable models go to Probabilistic Modelling; learned embeddings for downstream use go to Representation Learning:Embedding Methods.
example_children: Clustering; Dimensionality Reduction; Independent Component Analysis (ICA)

scope_in: Estimation and testing in the statistical tradition: regression models, survival analysis, high-dimensional inference, meta-analysis.
scope_out: Causal claims from observational data go to Causal Inference; probabilistic model building goes to Probabilistic Modelling.
example_children: Statistical Inference; Survival Analysis; Generalized Linear Models

scope_in: Work whose object is the training data itself: constructing, augmenting, cleaning, weighting or synthesising it.
scope_out: Datasets built to measure models go to concern:Benchmark Construction; the subject matter of the data goes to the domain axis; formal privacy of the data goes to concern:Privacy.
example_children: Data Augmentation; Synthetic Data; Data Curation

scope_in: Enlarging a training set by transformation or synthesis.
scope_out: Generative modelling studied for its own sake goes to Probabilistic Modelling:Deep Generative Modelling.
example_children: Data Augmentation; Text Data Augmentation; Synthetic Data

scope_in: Detecting and repairing defects in data: missingness, wrong labels, duplicates, inconsistent records.
scope_out: Robustness of a model to noisy labels during training goes to Training Regimes:Weakly Supervised Learning.
example_children: Data Cleaning in Machine Learning; Data Imputation; Label Cleaning

scope_in: Deciding which examples to keep, weight or mine, given a fixed pool.
scope_out: Deciding which examples to label goes to Training Regimes:Data-Efficient Learning.
example_children: Data Valuation; Data Reweighting; Hard Negative Mining
notes: Smallest method child I kept; three data names support it but only just.

scope_in: Estimating or discovering cause-effect relations and the assumptions under which they are identified.
scope_out: Correlational prediction goes to Classical Machine Learning Methods; latent factors without an interventional claim go to Representation Learning.
example_children: Causal Inference; Causal Discovery; CATE Estimation
notes: Only two children, which is the minimum; I did not invent a third.

scope_in: Quantifying the effect of an intervention or treatment from observational or interventional data.
scope_out: Recovering the graph rather than an effect goes to Causal Structure Discovery.
example_children: CATE Estimation; Interventional Data Analysis; Causal Inference in Social Networks

scope_in: Recovering the causal graph or mechanism set from data.
scope_out: Learning on a graph that is given goes to modality:Graph-Structured Data.
example_children: Causal Discovery; Structure Learning; Gene Regulatory Network Inference

scope_in: Work whose object is the structure of the learned latent space: disentanglement, identifiability, object factorisation, geometry, embeddings.
scope_out: The training signal that produced the representation goes to Training Regimes; the network that computes it goes to Neural Architecture Design; the data it represents goes to the modality axis.
example_children: Representation Learning; Disentanglement; Metric Learning
notes: Representation Learning is 56 papers and spawns a large modality-crossed tail (visual, video, graph, protein, audio-text), which is itself evidence for the multi-axis design.

scope_in: Recovering latent factors that vary independently, and the conditions under which they are identifiable.
scope_out: Interventions and effect estimation go to Causal Inference.
example_children: Disentanglement; Identifiable Representation Learning; Nonlinear Independent Component Analysis

scope_in: Learning latents that are claimed to correspond to causal mechanisms or to be identifiable up to a causal equivalence class.
scope_out: Effect estimation on observed variables goes to Causal Inference:Causal Effect Estimation.
example_children: Causal Representation Learning; Causal Feature Learning; Identifiability Theory
notes: A local speciality of this corpus (8 papers on the exact term). In another corpus this would be a leaf of Causal Inference.

scope_in: Decomposing a scene or input into discrete entities or slots.
scope_out: Detecting or segmenting objects with supervision goes to modality:Image Recognition.
example_children: Object-Centric Learning; Object-Centric Representations; Unsupervised Object Discovery

scope_in: Producing vectors whose geometry encodes similarity: metric learning, sparse and discrete codes, embedding spaces for retrieval.
scope_out: Retrieval systems as products go to domain:Search Systems.
example_children: Metric Learning; Text Embeddings; Graph Embedding

scope_in: Formal analysis of learning: generalisation, sample complexity, expressivity, convergence, and measured scaling behaviour.
scope_out: Empirical studies of training behaviour go to Optimization:Deep Learning Optimization; the algorithm being analysed goes to its own method category.
example_children: Machine Learning Theory; Generalization Bounds; Statistical Learning Theory
notes: Empirical Scaling Laws is placed here although it is measured, not proved; it answers the same question about how learning behaves with resources.

scope_in: Bounds and characterisations of the gap between training and test error.
scope_out: Generalisation under a shifted test distribution goes to concern:Robustness to Distribution Shift.
example_children: Generalization Bounds; PAC-Bayesian Theory; Sample Complexity

scope_in: What functions a network family can represent, and the analytic devices used to say so.
scope_out: Designing an architecture to gain a capability goes to Neural Architecture Design.
example_children: Network Expressivity; Neural Tangent Kernel; ReLU Networks

scope_in: Proofs about whether and how fast an iterative learning or optimisation procedure converges.
scope_out: Proposing the algorithm itself goes to Optimization.
example_children: Convergence Analysis; Algorithm Convergence; Stochastic Convex Optimization

scope_in: Measured relationships between model size, data, compute and performance.
scope_out: Engineering that makes large-scale training feasible goes to concern:Training Scalability.
example_children: Scaling Laws; Deep Learning Scaling Laws; Language Model Scaling

scope_in: Work whose contribution is an architectural component or inductive bias in its own right.
scope_out: A name that only states the backbone used (Transformers, Convolutional Neural Networks, Graph Neural Networks, Autoencoders) is not a research topic here: it goes to Not Specified on this axis and is recorded on the modality axis instead. Automatic search over architectures goes to Optimization:Black-Box Optimization; shrinking an architecture goes to concern:Model Compression.
example_children: Equivariant Neural Networks; Mixture of Experts; Neuromorphic Computing
notes: This is my answer to the architecture question: architectures are not a research area in this survey, but architecture DESIGN is. 28 backbone-only names cover 161 paper-mentions (2.7%); 76 of those are Graph Neural Networks, which the modality axis captures as graph data, leaving ~1.4% of mentions in the Not Specified bucket to be excluded in favour of the project’s separate architecture ontology.

scope_in: Architectures built around a symmetry or geometric structure of the input.
scope_out: The geometry of the learned latent space goes to Representation Learning.
example_children: Equivariant Neural Networks; Geometric Deep Learning; Equivariance in Neural Networks

scope_in: Architectures that route inputs to a subset of parameters: mixtures of experts, gating, modularity, dynamic depth or width.
scope_out: Static sparsification for speed goes to concern:Model Compression.
example_children: Mixture of Experts; Modular Neural Networks; Gating Mechanisms

scope_in: Architectures and hardware whose design argument is a biological mechanism.
scope_out: Using networks to model measured neural data goes to domain:Computational Neuroscience.
example_children: Neuromorphic Computing; Reservoir Computing; Neuroscience-inspired AI
notes: Smallest branch of this parent; retained because its three names are unplaceable elsewhere.

scope_in: Learning, emulating or solving the time evolution of a physical or mechanistic system.
scope_out: Forecasting an observed series with no mechanistic model goes to modality:Time Series Forecasting; controlling a system whose dynamics are given goes to Sequential Decision-Making:Control Theory.
example_children: Dynamical Systems; Physics-Informed Neural Networks; Neural Differential Equations
notes: Small (~25 names) but unmergeable: it is the only method family whose object is a differential equation rather than a dataset.

scope_in: Networks that solve or approximate solution operators of differential equations.
scope_out: Numerical analysis with no learned component goes to domain:Physical Sciences.
example_children: Neural Operators; Partial Differential Equation Solvers; Physics-Informed Neural Networks

scope_in: Learned fast approximations of an expensive simulator.
scope_out: Inference about simulator parameters goes to Probabilistic Modelling:Bayesian Inference.
example_children: Surrogate Modeling; Climate Model Emulation; Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs)

scope_in: Recovering the governing dynamics or operator of a system from observed trajectories.
scope_out: Recovering a causal graph over variables goes to Causal Inference:Causal Structure Discovery.
example_children: System Identification; Koopman Operators; Inverse Dynamics Modeling

scope_in: Names that state no technical method: bare umbrellas (Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Artificial Intelligence), pure application or field names, and backbone-only architecture names.
scope_out: Anything naming a family of algorithms, objectives or analyses belongs in one of the eleven method categories, however briefly it is stated.
example_children: Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Transformer Networks
notes: Residual bucket, measured: 40 contentless umbrella names account for 517 of 5990 paper-mentions (8.6%); backbone-only names add ~1.4%. Names filed here are usually informative on another axis, so they are not lost.

scope_in: Work on text, on linguistic structure, or on the behaviour of models of text.
scope_out: Source code goes to Source Code; spoken audio goes to Acoustic Signals; text paired with images goes to Multimodal Data.
example_children: Natural Language Processing; Language Modeling; Machine Translation
notes: Natural Language Processing is the single most frequent name in the corpus (295 papers).

scope_in: Tasks whose output is a label, span, structure or answer derived from given text.
scope_out: Producing new text goes to Language Generation; ranking documents for a user goes to domain:Search Systems.
example_children: Question Answering; Natural Language Inference; Named Entity Recognition

scope_in: Tasks whose output is text: translation, summarisation, dialogue, controlled and conditional generation.
scope_out: Generic generative-model methodology goes to method:Deep Generative Modelling.
example_children: Text Generation; Text Summarization; Dialogue Systems

scope_in: Language studied as an object: syntax, semantics, pragmatics, sociolinguistics, grammar.
scope_out: Engineering a parser to improve a downstream task goes to Language Understanding.
example_children: Syntax; Dependency Parsing; Lexical Semantics

scope_in: Work whose difficulty is the number of languages or the scarcity of data in them.
scope_out: Transfer machinery studied independently of language goes to method:Transfer Learning.
example_children: Multilingual NLP; Low-Resource Languages; Multilingual Models

scope_in: Study and steering of large pretrained language models as objects: prompting, in-context learning, reasoning traces, retrieval augmentation, factual recall.
scope_out: Opening the model to explain its computation goes to concern:Mechanistic Interpretability; efficiency of serving it goes to concern:Computational Efficiency.
example_children: Large Language Models; In-Context Learning; Prompt Engineering
notes: A modality child rather than a method: in this corpus these names always presuppose text, and their claims are about a text model’s behaviour.

scope_in: Work on images, video, or 3D visual structure.
scope_out: Images of molecules or graphs drawn as pictures are rare here; molecular and graph data go to their own categories. Rendering as an end product goes to domain:Computer Graphics.
example_children: Computer Vision; Image Classification; Semantic Segmentation
notes: Computer Vision is 240 papers, the 4th most frequent name. Six children, justified by the size and breadth of the visual tail.

scope_in: Assigning labels, boxes or masks to the content of an image.
scope_out: Detecting that an image is out of distribution goes to concern:Out-of-Distribution Detection; medical images go to Biomedical Imaging.
example_children: Image Classification; Object Detection; Semantic Segmentation

scope_in: Producing or editing image content.
scope_out: Text-conditioned image generation goes to Multimodal Data:Text-to-Image Generation; the generative machinery itself goes to method:Deep Generative Modelling.
example_children: Image Generation; Image-to-Image Translation; Image Editing

scope_in: Work whose difficulty is the temporal dimension of visual data.
scope_out: Non-visual time series go to Temporal Signals.
example_children: Video Prediction; Object Tracking; Activity Recognition

scope_in: Representing, reconstructing or rendering three-dimensional geometry: meshes, point clouds, radiance fields, depth, SLAM mapping.
scope_out: 3D molecular geometry goes to Biomolecular Data; robot navigation using a map goes to domain:Robot Navigation.
example_children: 3D Reconstruction; Neural Radiance Fields; Point Cloud Processing

scope_in: Images acquired from living systems and the pipelines specific to them: MRI, CT, PET, ultrasound, microscopy, histology, radiomics.
scope_out: The clinical question the image answers goes to domain:Health; brain-mapping analyses go to domain:Human Brain Mapping.
example_children: Medical Imaging; Neuroimaging; Microscopy
notes: Roughly 60 names, the densest single cluster in the corpus tail. Splitting it across Image Recognition and domain:Health would have destroyed it.

scope_in: Operations on the image signal itself: registration, reconstruction, deconvolution, compression, denoising.
scope_out: Semantic content extraction goes to Image Recognition.
example_children: Image Registration; Image Compression; Image Deconvolution

scope_in: Work on sound: speech, music, and environmental or biological audio.
scope_out: Text transcripts analysed without audio go to Natural Language; general one-dimensional signals go to Temporal Signals.
example_children: Speech Recognition; Speech Processing; Audio Classification

scope_in: Mapping speech audio to text or to speaker-independent linguistic labels.
scope_out: Producing speech goes to Speech Synthesis; identifying who is speaking goes to Speaker Modelling.
example_children: Automatic Speech Recognition; Speech-to-Text Translation; Accent Classification

scope_in: Producing or modifying speech audio: text-to-speech, enhancement, separation, voice editing.
scope_out: Generative-model methodology goes to method:Deep Generative Modelling.
example_children: Text-to-Speech (TTS); Speech Enhancement; Speech Separation

scope_in: Characterising the speaker rather than the content: verification, embeddings, paralinguistics.
scope_out: Emotion inferred from text goes to Natural Language:Language Understanding.
example_children: Speaker Verification; Speaker Embedding; Speech Emotion Recognition

scope_in: Audio work whose object is music.
scope_out: Recommending music to users goes to domain:Recommender Systems.
example_children: Music Generation; Music Source Separation; Music Information Retrieval (MIR)

scope_in: Work whose data are nodes and edges: molecular, citation, social, biological, knowledge and temporal graphs.
scope_out: Graphs used as a probabilistic model of dependence go to method:Probabilistic Graphical Models; molecules treated chemically rather than as graphs go to Biomolecular Data.
example_children: Graph Neural Networks; Graph Learning; Node Classification
notes: Graph Neural Networks (76 papers) is recorded here rather than as an architecture: the name reliably tells you the data are graphs, which is exactly what this axis measures.

scope_in: Predicting attributes of individual nodes.
scope_out: Predicting a property of the whole graph goes to Graph-Level Prediction.
example_children: Node Classification; Semi-Supervised Node Classification; Graph Anomaly Detection (GAD)

scope_in: Predicting the existence or evolution of edges.
scope_out: Reasoning over typed relations in a knowledge base goes to Knowledge Graphs.
example_children: Link Prediction; Dynamic Link Prediction; Graph Recovery

scope_in: Predicting a property of an entire graph, and comparing graphs.
scope_out: Molecular property prediction, where the chemistry is the point, goes to Biomolecular Data.
example_children: Graph Classification; Graph Regression; Graph Kernels

scope_in: Graphs whose structure changes over time.
scope_out: Static graphs with time-varying node features only go to Node-Level Prediction.
example_children: Temporal Graph Learning; Dynamic Graphs; Temporal Network Models

scope_in: Typed, symbolic relational stores and reasoning over them, including ontologies and taxonomies.
scope_out: Untyped network structure goes to Link Prediction; factual recall inside a language model goes to Language Model Behaviour.
example_children: Knowledge Graphs; Knowledge Graph Reasoning; Ontology Alignment

scope_in: Work whose data are molecules, proteins, nucleic acids, cells or omics measurements.
scope_out: The biological question being answered goes to domain:Life Sciences; generic graph methodology goes to Graph-Structured Data.
example_children: Molecular Property Prediction; Protein Structure Prediction; Single-cell Analysis
notes: Justified as a modality rather than folded into the Life Sciences domain because the corpus has ~90 names for tasks defined on these data, independent of the biology being studied.

scope_in: Predicting physical, chemical or biological properties of small molecules.
scope_out: Proposing new molecules goes to Molecular Design.
example_children: Molecular Property Prediction; Molecular Representations; Molecule Classification

scope_in: Generating or optimising molecules, sequences and synthesis routes toward a target property.
scope_out: Drug development as a pipeline and its clinical goals go to domain:Drug Discovery.
example_children: Molecule Generation; RNA Design; Retrosynthetic Planning

scope_in: Structure, function, interaction and language models of proteins and peptides.
scope_out: Immunological questions go to domain:Immunology.
example_children: Protein Structure Prediction; Protein Language Models; Protein-Ligand Binding

scope_in: Modelling systems at the level of atoms and their interactions.
scope_out: The learned-operator machinery goes to method:Dynamical Systems Modelling; materials questions go to domain:Materials Science.
example_children: Molecular Dynamics (MD); Quantum Mechanics (QM); 3D Atomic Systems

scope_in: Measurements at single-cell resolution and their integration across assays.
scope_out: Population-level genomics goes to domain:Genomics.
example_children: Single-cell Analysis; Single-Cell Transcriptomics; Single-Cell Multi-Omics

scope_in: Work on one-dimensional measurements ordered in time that are neither speech nor video.
scope_out: Sequential decision-making goes to method:Sequential Decision-Making; video goes to Visual Data:Video Understanding.
example_children: Time Series Forecasting; Time Series Analysis; Signal Processing

scope_in: Predicting future values of a measured series.
scope_out: Predicting the evolution of a physically modelled system goes to method:Dynamical Systems Modelling.
example_children: Probabilistic Forecasting; Renewable Energy Forecasting; Data-Driven Forecasting

scope_in: Finding unusual points, segments or change points in a series.
scope_out: The reliability question of whether a model should abstain goes to concern:Out-of-Distribution Detection.
example_children: Time-Series Anomaly Detection; Log-based Anomaly Detection; Bayesian Change Point Detection
notes: Genuinely straddles this axis and concern:Anomaly Detection; the rule is that the series is the data here, the trust question is there.

scope_in: Electrophysiological and physiological recordings: EEG, MEG, ECG, and their decoding.
scope_out: Brain images rather than traces go to Visual Data:Biomedical Imaging; the neuroscience question goes to domain:Neuroscience.
example_children: EEG Analysis; Electroencephalography; Biomedical Signal Processing

scope_in: Work whose difficulty is the joint use of two or more data types.
scope_out: One data type processed by several models is not multimodal; several tasks on one data type go to method:Multi-Task Learning.
example_children: Multimodal Learning; Vision-Language Models; Visual Question Answering
